I farm for a living, and on 16.9 mu with six people in the household and some labor going off-farm, I will keep my plan practical and steady. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most reliable way for me to use the land, spread labor across the year, and make use of my well irrigation. I will keep a smaller part in cotton because I already grow it and it gives me another source of income, but I will not expand it too much because cotton takes more careful field management and more pesticide work. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and a few irrigations to secure tillering, jointing, and grain filling. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land because hybrid maize gives me stable yield and fits the local system well. For cotton, I will use hybrid seed, a bit more potassium, and more pesticide sprays than grain crops because insects and boll protection matter. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and is enough for my scale, while keeping yields stable.
